title: Speculative decoding: proposal-scoring telemetry and staged fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a pragmatic speculative decoding runtime component that 1) proposes candidate model/decoder lanes for each request using a lightweight scoring function, 2) computes an online acceptance confidence metric for speculative outputs, and 3) orchestrates graceful fallback to full decode when acceptance confidence is low or computational resources are constrained. This ticket covers the runtime policy, telemetry surface, and staged rollout strategy. It explicitly focuses on interactions with kernel selection, attention-prefill vs decode scheduling, and cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request candidate scoring is emitted to tracing with <10us median overhead
Acceptance metric computed for each speculative chunk (prefill+first n tokens) and available to the router within 2ms after chunk completion
Fallback trigger reduces user-facing incorrect speculative outputs by >=90% on flagged prompts (based on eval suite)
End-to-end 99th percentile latency for decodes when speculative path used does not increase by >10% versus baseline decode-only path
Operational dashboard shows acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, avg_latency_delta, and cost_delta per model variant
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight ModelProposal struct (model_id, kernel_profile_hint, proposer_score, estimated_cost) serialized into request metadata
Scoring function initial form: logistic combination of short-form prefix match score (string/embedding sketch), recent per-model acceptance_smoothed, and kernel_latency_hint

Acceptance metric: two-part signal: (a) topk-token-agreement heuristic over first N tokens, (b) model-confidence delta (LM logit-gap) normalized by temperature — combine into single confidence score with configurable thresholds
Prefill scheduling: run prefill of proposed fast variant in low-priority micro-batches while primary prefill runs; prefer KV cache reuse if model architecture matches

Decode scheduling: issue speculative decode on fast-path kernel using continuous-batching; schedule a parallel conservative decode only when confidence < threshold OR when compute budget allows for parallelism
Fallback: when conservative decode completes or acceptance fails, atomically swap response; ensure token-ids correspond (use sequence-reconciliation step) to avoid hallucinated continuations
Kernel selection: proposal should include kernel affinity tags to avoid expensive kernel switch during mid-request; prefer proposals that preserve KV layout
Config knobs: per-customer allowed speculative risk (none/low/medium/high), per-model min_acceptance_threshold, max_parallel_budget_tokens
Roll-forward experiments gated under 'spec-decode' feature flag per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit tests + deterministic eval harness against curated prompt set (perf/regression)
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal traffic only; expose telemetry to runtime dashboard; run for 72h
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 10% of low-risk customers with opt-in flag; collect acceptance/fallback metrics and manual QA
Phase 3 (ramp): gradually increase to 50% of eligible traffic with automated rollback if fallback_rate > 2x baseline or client-facing error increases
Phase 4 (GA): make feature available as configurable runtime policy with per-customer knobs
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created. Initial design doc linked. Decided to keep proposer lightweight to minimize prefill overhead.
2025-02-18: Prototype scoring function implemented in python harness. Early results: ~0.6 acceptance on small eval; needs calibration.
2025-02-24: Kernel-affinity tagging design reviewed with infra (Sanjay). Concern: frequent kernel switches increased tail latency during stress tests.
2025-02-27: Implemented atomic response swap prototype with sequence-reconciliation. Added reconciler to handle token-id remapping for fused tokenizers.
2025-03-01: Instrumentation hooks added to runtime tracing. Baseline overhead measured: 7us median per request. Preparing canary rollout plan.
